text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Greece puts in a strong presence at the Nikiforos military exercise.
- The United States is expected to submit a new proposal for a military dialogue between the two sides in Cyprus soon.
- Woman who is writing an 'uncensored' book on the Duchess of York had a Cypriot husband.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Lord Finsberg, the Council of Europe rapporteur on Cyprus, dies aged 70.
- Police take new working hours dispute to the Supreme Court.
- House of Representatives Finance Committee protests its poor cooperation with the finance ministry on Cyprus Airways issues.
- British bases are to axe more than 150 jobs.
HARAVGHI
- Parliamentarians are to suggest legislation giving citizens access to public documents.
- Police fume over new working hours.
- Prices of imported cheeses are set to rise.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Washington will launch its initiative on Cyprus first by concentrating on getting a military dialogue between the two sides off the ground.
- Two of Cyprus' largest private colleges will merge.
- Draft legislation which will be tabled soon to parliament penalises smuggling of goods from the Turkish-occupied areas.
SIMERINI
- Justice minister warns he will take disciplinary action against policemen who refuse to conform with new working hours.
- Greece participates in the Nikiforos military exercise.
